advice: Propose simplifying only the K-loop counter in `Llibxsmm_478` and `Llibxsmm_70c`: the supplied current assembly has one K step per iteration, so replace each 512-step countdown with an end-pointer test. Set an end pointer from the loop’s initial operand pointer plus the full span: 1,048,576 bytes for B (`x0`, 2048-byte step) and 131,072 bytes for packed A (`x3`, 256-byte step). After each iteration’s existing loads, pointer updates, and four ordered FP32 FMOPA operations, loop while both streams have not reached their ends. Keep the existing pointer rewinds and all other traversal unchanged. This is distinct from the prior proposal and measured pointer-end variant: it tests a joint two-stream termination check, not separate single-stream checks. The hypothesis that it reduces loop-control work is unverified.
risks: The exact initial pointers and stride arithmetic must match each loop, including the second output half’s packed-A start. Preserve exactly 512 ordered updates, do not load past either stream, and ensure the end values survive the loop without conflicting with live registers. Changing loop control may add instructions or regress performance. Verify the source against the supplied assembly, then check full GEMM correctness at n=512 and the general-size boundary set, including odd sizes, tails, and n<=0. Keep the fixed ABI, FP32 arithmetic, tolerance, thread count, flags, timed work, and complete license notice. Measure with fresh paired controls under unchanged power settings; do not claim a gain or attribute noisy outcomes to this change alone.
